 Nvidia Uncertainty Deepens Hong Kong’s Tech Rout, Hang Seng Sheds 844 Points
 By Business Today Editorial 
 November 15, 2026 
 Share 
 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin 
 Hong Kong equities suffered a sharp sell-off over the Nov 9 to 13 week, with the Hang Seng Index (HSI) losing 844.31 points or 3.45% to close at 23,637.60, as technology stocks came under pressure amid renewed concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) investments and uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.
 The benchmark ended below the psychologically important 24,000 level, retreating from 24,481.91 at the previous week’s close. The decline was concentrated in the final two trading sessions, when the index shed a combined 844.31 points. 
 The HSI fell 473.36 points or 1.93% on Nov 12 to 24,008.55, before dropping another 370.95 points or 1.55% on Friday. The two sessions left the index with three consecutive days of losses, extending the pressure on Hong Kong equities.
 Technology and semiconductor counters led the retreat, as concerns over the sustainability of AI-related investment and Nvidia leadership uncertainty unsettled investors. The weakness in the sector also weighed on other major Asian technology stocks.
 On Friday, 80 of the HSI’s 94 constituents ended lower. Lenovo Group was among the worst performers, plunging 6.33%, while Hua Hong Semiconductor fell 6.1%. Xiaomi Corporation declined 3.74%, Alibaba Group lost 3.46% and Tencent Holdings shed 3%.
 Property stocks also faced selling pressure, with Longfor Group falling 6.43% to become the worst-performing Hang Seng blue chip.
 The Hang Seng Tech Index bore the brunt of the sell-off, dropping 118.74 points or 3.02% to 3,813.19 on Friday. Its weekly decline reached nearly 6.5%, marking its steepest weekly fall since June 26.
 The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index also retreated, shedding 119.23 points or 1.48% to 7,937.53, while the Red Chip Index fell 65.33 points or 1.64% to 3,915.
 Not all sectors moved lower. Energy stocks offered some resistance to the broader decline, supported by stronger oil prices amid heightened geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. PetroChina gained 2.79%, while China Petroleum and Chemical Corporation advanced 1.71%.
 Paper and packaging, alongside oil and petrochemicals, were also among the few market themes to strengthen against the broader downturn. However, gains in these areas were insufficient to offset the losses in technology and other major sectors.
 The week’s trading was limited to two sessions, with the market closed on Nov 9 and Nov 10 due to public holidays. Trading resumed on Nov 12, when the HSI suffered its sharpest daily decline of the week.
 The sell-off came after the index had been expected to trade within a range of 24,000 to 24,500. However, concerns over AI investment prospects, semiconductor valuations and Nvidia-related uncertainty pushed the benchmark below that range.
 With the HSI ending the week at 23,637.60, investors will be watching whether the index can regain the 24,000 level, while developments in global technology sentiment and geopolitical conditions are likely to remain important influences on market direction.
